note: Arduino Uno works as a drop-in code substitute for Nano (requires slightly more space).
Arduino Nano has the same ATmega328P core and pin capabilities on a breadboard.
ESP32 provides full Wi-Fi support with surplus GPIOs and Bluetooth.
ESP8266 handles Wi-Fi connectivity though has fewer analog pins.
0.96" I2C OLED can display text/metrics with smaller footprint.
16x2 I2C LCD displays textual telemetry in place of graphic OLED.
Standard 5V phone charger delivers stable 5V DC via cut USB cable.
5V 2A DC barrel jack adapter supplies identical 5V regulated power.
8-Ohm mini speaker can generate square wave tones using PWM output.
Laptop blower fan motor spins with 5V DC for airflow experiments.
9V battery can power microcontroller via VIN through linear regulator.
18650 Li-ion cell (with boost converter) provides cleaner sustained current.
Stepper motor with driver can perform indexed rotational positioning.
Most phone chargers include detachable USB cables.
